Subject: Re: Quick follow-up and pricing sketch from today's call

Thanks again for taking the time today — great conversation and helpful context on where ZenPay wants to land on cost per transaction and procurement cadence. Quick recap + ask so we can get you a clean SOW for procurement: 

Recap from the call:
- Primary integration: conversational payment assistant for merchant support (high-value escalations).
- Expected traffic profile: 50k–200k daily sessions initially, average 300 tokens/session for prompt+response (rough estimate).
- Target latency: <=400ms tail for critical flows; can tolerate slightly higher for non-critical.

We discussed unit economics and your procurement thresholds — specifically you mentioned procurement prefers to keep vendor spend under $50k on self-serve contracts to avoid a full PO process. If ZenPay expects to stay below that threshold month-to-month, we can support a shorter SOW; above that we will need a PO and the usual procurement timelines (typically 30–60 days).

Attached is a quick pricing sketch (redwood_pricing_estimate_Q2.pdf) with 3 monthly bands based on tokens/month. Can you confirm two things so I can finalize for your procurement team:  
1) Approx monthly token volume you expect in the 0–3mo pilot (low/med/high from your perspective).
2) Procurement threshold we should price to (is $50k/month the hard cutoff, or is $25k/quarter the internal target?).

Proposed next steps:
- You confirm token band + procurement target (reply inline)
- I’ll send a draft SOW + pricing table and loop in Legal/Procurement as needed
- If helpful, schedule a 30-minute procurement sync next week

Thanks — I’ll hold on the formal SOW until I get your confirmation so we price to the right band.

Best,

Thanks Marissa — huge appreciation for the clear recap. Quick answers inline below: 

1) Pilot token volume: we expect the pilot (month 1) to be ~60M tokens, month 2 ramp to 180M tokens, steady state 350–450M tokens/month depending on conversion. The 300 tokens/session estimate matches our internal numbers.

2) Procurement threshold: our procurement prefers not to open a formal PO for vendors under $50k/month. For anything above that, we will require a PO and vendor onboarding (legal + security questionnaire). Our finance team will likely ask for net 30 or net 45 terms.

For pricing, we are targeting a blended cost of <= $75 per 1M tokens (target), ideally closer to $50 per 1M for cost-sensitive paths. If we can get to that at scale (>300M tokens/month), we can more easily justify an annual commit.

I attached our procurement checklist (zenpay_procurement_requirements.docx) so you can see where we typically get hung up. Next: please send your refined pricing bands that map to the token volumes above and indicate what requires PO vs self-serve.

—Samir

Subject: Re: Budget range validation: draft pricing bands + procurement notes

Samir — thanks for the fast reply and for the procurement checklist. Per your ask, I’ve sketched 3 pricing bands tied to monthly token usage plus the procurement trigger points. These numbers are preliminary (pilot pricing + optional volume discounts) — I’ll convert to a formal SOW once you confirm the target band.

Pricing sketch (all $ per 1M tokens):
- Pilot (0–100M tokens/month): $140 per 1M tokens (includes pilot support, monitoring, basic caching)
- Scale (100–300M tokens/month): $95 per 1M tokens (volume discount + optimized batching recommendations)
- Enterprise (300M+ tokens/month): $60 per 1M tokens (committed throughput pricing, reserved capacity options)

Example monthly spend bands (approx):
- 60M tokens: ~ $8,400/month (pilot band)
- 180M tokens: ~ $17,100/month (mix of pilot->scale; we would price to scale band for committed months)
- 400M tokens: ~ $24,000/month (enterprise band)

Procurement triggers and options:
- Self-serve/SOW under $50k/month: we can onboard under our standard hosted terms (no PO required) and support via the account team; payment terms typically net 30.
- PO required: for expected monthly spend >= $50k, we will need a signed PO; onboarding timeline typically 30–60 days (legal + security review).
- Reserved capacity/annual commit: for customers who want committed capacity and lower unit pricing we offer monthly/annual reserved contracts with SLAs; these usually require procurement + PO.

Notes on unit economics and ops levers:
- We can reduce effective $/1M via batching + prefix caching for high-reuse prompts — Dylan has some suggested engineering changes that can typically save 15–30% on token spend.
- If you have multiple models (cheaper model for non-critical flows), we can route lower priority traffic to a cost-optimized variant.

Proposed next steps:
1) Confirm which band you want us to price to for the SOW (pilot/scale/enterprise).
2) If PO is required, share procurement contact and preferred timeline so we can align Legal.
3) Schedule a 30-min technical deep-dive with Dylan to capture batching/embedding tradeoffs (Dylan, can you be available early next week?).

If these bands look reasonable, I’ll send the draft SOW mapped to your target band and include explicit payment/PO language. Happy to adjust numbers if you have a different target $/1M.

Best,

Marissa Cole

Quick technical note from my side — appreciate the numbers and target $/1M. A couple items that will materially move the needle on effective cost: 

- Batching & concurrency tuning: enabling continuous batching with our runtime can reduce per-token compute by ~10–20% for your traffic shape (short prompts, many parallel sessions).
- Prefix KV caching: for repeated merchant/faq prompts we typically see 20–40% reduction in tokens sent to the model.
- Model routing: route non-critical/low-sensitivity flows to a smaller model variant (same API surface) — this often halves token unit cost for those flows.

If ZenPay wants to target $50–75 per 1M tokens at scale, the combination of reserved capacity + the above application changes is realistic. Happy to run a quick cost-savings simulation if you send a week of anonymized traffic (token counts by flow).
